description: Fig. 5 is a six-panel group of optical micrographs (OM) of etched Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel annealed for 1 h, imaged on two orthogonal sections; every panel carries a 50 µm scale bar. (a), (c) and (e) are RD–ND sections (ND/RD orientation arrows) showing the banded structure at 800, 850 and 900 °C respectively: elongated bright α strips (red arrow) alternate with finer two-phase bands; orange arrows mark κ-carbide, labelled K, in (a) and (c). (b), (d) and (f) are RD–TD sections (TD/RD arrows) at the same three temperatures and resolve the constituent phases more clearly: blue arrows mark γ, red α, orange κ. At 800 °C (b) dark κ particles and networks occupy boundaries between α and γ areas and along α/α boundaries within the large α regions. At 850 °C (d) the γ areas appear cleaner and κ is largely confined to the continuous dark boundary networks. At 900 °C (e, f) no κ-carbide is labelled or apparent, and α/γ grains look coarser and more equiaxed. Together the panels argue that κ-carbide progressively dissolves between 800 and 900 °C while the banded α structure persists but becomes less contiguous.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, RD–ND section, labelled '800 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, ND/RD axis arrows. Shows strongly banded structure of elongated bright α strips (red arrow labelled α) separated by dark, finely etched two-phase bands; an orange arrow labels κ-carbide as K.

Optical micrograph, RD–TD section, labelled '800 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, TD/RD arrows. Bright γ areas (blue arrow) and α (red arrow) are outlined by dark κ-carbide networks, with two orange K arrows marking κ between α and γ areas and decorating boundaries.

Optical micrograph, RD–ND section, labelled '850 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, ND/RD arrows. Banded structure of bright α strips (red arrow) remains; a blue arrow marks γ and an orange K arrow marks κ-carbide.

Optical micrograph, RD–TD section, labelled '850 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, TD/RD arrows. γ islands (blue arrow) and α (red arrow) are surrounded by continuous dark κ-carbide networks; two orange K arrows point to κ-carbide, which is now concentrated on the boundary networks rather than dispersed in the γ areas.

Optical micrograph, RD–ND section, labelled '900 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, ND/RD arrows. Banded structure persists but the bands are less continuous and coarser; only α (red arrow) and γ (blue arrow) are labelled — no κ-carbide marker is present.

Optical micrograph, RD–TD section, labelled '900 °C, 1 h', 50 µm scale bar, TD/RD arrows. Coarser, more equiaxed α (red arrow) and γ (blue arrow) grains; no κ-carbide label and no obvious κ particles visible.

observations.observation: All six panels carry a 50 µm scale bar and a section/orientation compass (ND–RD for (a)(c)(e), TD–RD for (b)(d)(f)).
Panels are labelled in their top-right corner with the annealing condition '800 °C, 1 h' (a, b), '850 °C, 1 h' (c, d) and '900 °C, 1 h' (e, f).
The caption states that (a)(c)(e) show the microstructures of the RD–ND section and (b)(d)(f) the microstructures of the RD–TD section.
Panel (a) shows a strongly banded RD–ND structure with a red arrow labelling α on a long bright strip and an orange arrow labelling κ-carbide as K.
In panel (b) (800 °C, RD–TD) dark κ-carbide is marked by two orange K arrows and occurs between α and γ areas and along boundaries, while the blue arrow marks γ and the red arrow marks α.
In panel (d) (850 °C, RD–TD) the dark κ-carbide is confined to continuous boundary networks around the clean γ and α areas, with two orange K arrows and one blue γ arrow.
Panels (e) and (f) (900 °C) contain only red α and blue γ arrows, with no κ-carbide (K) label present anywhere in the frame.
The citing text states that the banded structure and long strip α phase remain in Fig. 5(a), (c) and (e).
The citing text states that the dissolution temperature of κ-carbide is between 850 °C and 900 °C, as obtained from the OM micrographs in Fig. 5.
The citing text states that at 900 °C (Fig. 5(f)) no obvious κ-carbide can be seen, i.e. κ-carbide has almost dissolved into the α and γ matrices.
The citing text states that the banded structure becomes less contiguous at higher temperatures (Figs. 5(a), (c), (e)).

Discrepancy to flag: the citing text attributes the 800 °C discussion to 'Fig. 5(d)', whereas the caption and the printed panel label identify (d) as the 850 °C specimen; both readings are reported and neither is confirmed by the other.
The citing text states that the microstructural trend with temperature shown by SEM (Fig. 6) is clearer than the comparison of the OM micrographs of the two specimens in Fig. 5(b) and (d).

unreadable_items: No phase fractions, particle sizes or grain sizes are printed on any panel; only temperatures, times and the 50 µm scale bar are labelled
Individual κ-carbide particles in (b) and (d) cannot be counted or sized reliably at the supplied resolution — only their spatial distribution (boundary networks vs. dispersed) is legible
Etching contrast between α and γ in the RD–ND panels (a)(c)(e) is weak, so the two phases cannot be separated by eye there without the printed arrows
